headline_marked: DU students' [[residential seats cancelled over homosexuality]] allegations
headline: DU students' residential seats cancelled over homosexuality allegations
summary: Two students of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall have been permanently expelled from the residency after allegations of homosexuality surfaced.
details: Two students of Dhaka University's Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall have had their residential seats permanently cancelled following allegations of homosexuality.
Hall Provost Professor Md. Akhtaruzzaman confirmed the action on Wednesday, stating that the seats were revoked permanently.
Ahmed Al Sabah, General Secretary of the Hall Parliament, announced the decision via Facebook, citing 'serious breach of social discipline' after evidence was found.
The students were immediately removed from the hall in the presence of their local guardians, and further disciplinary action through the university administration is being processed.
One of the accused students told Prothom Alo that they are currently experiencing 'trauma' and are unwilling to discuss the matter further.
This is not the first such incident; on July 30, a student from Masterda Surya Sen Hall was permanently expelled under similar allegations.

Additionally, recent allegations of the same nature surfaced at Shahidullah Hall involving two guests of the Assistant General Secretary of the Hall Parliament, leading to the temporary cancellation of the AGS's seat.

headline_marked: Severe [[gas crisis hits Chattogram]] as supply drops to half of demand
headline: Severe gas crisis hits Chattogram as supply drops to half of demand
summary: Residents face cooking struggles and CNG drivers endure long queues as bad weather prevents LNG ships from docking.
details: A severe gas shortage has struck Chattogram, leaving many households unable to cook and creating massive queues at CNG filling stations across the city.
The Karnaphuli Gas Distribution Company Limited (KGDCL) reported that supply has plummeted to 18-19 crore cubic feet, while the city's daily demand is approximately 35 crore cubic feet.
The crisis is caused by severe weather conditions in Maheshkhali, where wind speeds have reached 38 knots, far exceeding the 20-knot safety limit for LNG ships to dock.
Because the LNG tankers cannot berth at the floating terminals, the national grid supply has dropped, directly impacting the city's gas pressure.
Drivers of CNG-powered auto-rickshaws and private cars have reported waiting for hours at stations like Fossil Filling Station, with some finding supply completely shut off at others.
This follows a previous crisis in July caused by technical failures in a boiler at the floating terminals, which had been partially resolved before this weather-related shortage hit.
Petrobangla officials stated that once the LNG cargo ship can safely dock, the supply to the national grid could increase from 40 crore to 75 crore cubic feet.
Until the weather improves and the ships can berth, Chattogram will continue to operate with nearly half of its required gas supply.
